newsitem.title: USA: ABC wins Nielsen ratings for April 28-May 4.
newsitem.headline: ABC wins Nielsen ratings for April 28-May 4.

text.p: Walt Disney Co's ABC television network, powered by the Wednesday sitcom "Ellen," won top prime time television ratings for the week April 28 to May 4, Nielsen Media Research said Tuesday.

"Ellen" was the most watched prime time show during the week, garnering 23.4 rating points and a 35 percent share, said Nielsen, a unit of Cognizant Corp. The episode centered on a "coming out" for the show's star, comedienne Ellen DeGeneris, as a lesbian.

With three other shows -- newsmagazine "PrimeTime Live," "ABC Sunday Night Movie," and sitcom "Home Improvement" -- ABC gained 10.8 rating points and an 18 percent share for prime time audience viewership for the week, Nielsen said.
The three shows were the fourth, eighth and 10th among the 10 most-watched shows during the week.

NBC, a unit of General Electric Co, was second with 10.0 rating points and a 17 percent share. It had five shows that landed in the top 10 -- hospital drama series "E.R." (No. 2), and sitcoms "Seinfeld" (No. 3), "Friends" (No. 5),"Fired Up" (No.6) and "Suddenly Susan" (No. 7).

In third spot was CBS, a unit of Westinghouse Electric Corp, posting 9.5 rating points and 16 percent market share. The only show the network landed in the top 10 was the series "Touched by an Angel," which was at the 9th spot.
Fox, a News Corp Ltd unit, was fourth, logging 7.0 rating points and an 11 percent share.
Viacom Inc's UPN was fifth, with 3.1 rating points and a 5.0 percent share.
In sixth place was WB, a Time Warner Inc network, with 2.2 rating points and a four percent share.
The rating points represent a percentage of homes with televisions and the share represents sets tuned in at a particular time.
